n: The angel returns and rouses Zechariah as though from sleep, preparing him for vision five.

f.g: Roused him to full spiritual alertness.

n: He sees a golden lampstand with a bowl on top feeding seven lamps through pipes.

f.g: A lampstand (menorah), like the one in the tabernacle.

n: Two olive trees stand beside it, one on each side, supplying oil.
Zechariah asks what these things mean.
The angel asks if he understands; Zechariah honestly admits he doesn’t.

f.g: Humility opens the way for revelation.

n: The key message for Zerubbabel: the temple will be finished “not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.” Just as the lamp burns with a steady oil supply, God’s work goes forward by His Spirit.

f.w: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit

n: Every mountain-sized obstacle will become flat ground before Zerubbabel. He will set the final stone amid shouts of “Grace, grace to it!”

f.g: The top or capstone — the final stone marking completion.

n: Another word from the Lord comes to Zechariah.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: A formula introducing a new revelation.

n: Zerubbabel laid the temple foundation, and he will finish it. It was completed in 515 BC.

f.w: his hands shall also finish it

n: Don’t despise small beginnings! People will rejoice to see Zerubbabel holding the plumb line. The “seven” are the Lord’s eyes that see everything on earth.

f.w: who hath despised the day of small things?

f.g: Plumb line, or a special “tin stone” — a builder’s tool.

f.w: the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro

n: Zechariah asks about the two olive trees.

f.w: What are these two olive trees

n: He asks more specifically about two olive branches that pour golden oil through golden pipes.

f.g: Literally “the gold” — the gleaming olive oil.

n: Again the angel asks; again Zechariah admits he doesn’t know.

f.w: Knowest thou not what these be?
f.g: The repeated question deepens the anticipation.

n: They are “the two anointed ones” who stand by the Lord of all the earth — likely Zerubbabel (the royal leader) and Joshua (the high priest). Revelation uses the same image for two latter-day witnesses.

f.g: Literally “sons of oil” — the governor and the priest, both anointed to serve.

f.w: that stand by the Lord of the whole earth
